findings.text: The legacy DRM header exposes compatibility alias names for core user space types. Each alias names a corresponding record or enumeration for clip handling, drawable information, texture regions, hardware lock, version, unique identifier, list, block, control, mapping type and flags, context private mapping, mapping, client, statistics, lock and DMA descriptors, buffer management, vertical blank waiting, AGP modes and objects, contexts and results, drawing, authentication, interrupt bus identification, blank sequence typing and scatter gather setup. The fragment only declares the aliases and does not define member layouts or behavior.

The fourcc header uses a single preprocessor guard to prevent repeated inclusion. Once defined, further inclusion in the same translation unit has no additional effect and carries no runtime behavior.

Four character codes are built as unsigned thirty two bit values by placing the first supplied byte lowest and shifting later bytes by eight, sixteen and twenty four positions before combining. Identity follows ordered byte positions in little endian packing rather than host integer order.

Zero is reserved as an invalid format sentinel that never denotes a usable pixel layout. A separate high bit flag marks a variant whose multi byte components use big endian order instead of the default little endian order used by most packed formats.

Single component low depth formats pack several pixels per byte at decreasing density. One bit variants hold eight pixels per byte, two bit variants hold four, four bit variants hold two, and eight bit variants hold one component per byte. Separate families cover indexed, depth like and red like channels with shared densities.

Wider single and dual channel integer formats use sixteen or thirty two bit little endian containers. Ten, twelve and sixteen bit red only variants occupy sixteen bits with leading padding for narrower widths. Dual channel pairs store two eight bit channels in sixteen bits or two sixteen bit channels in thirty two bits, with channel order swapped between naming variants.

Low and medium depth packed color stores all channels in one value without alpha. One family packs red green and blue as three three and two bits in a single byte with channel order swapped between variants. Another family stores three eight bit channels contiguously in twenty four bits little endian, again with red first and blue first orderings.

Sixteen bit packed color combines four bit, five bit and five six five layouts little endian. Four bit per channel forms use sixteen bits for pad or alpha plus red green blue in several orders, with the extra nibble at either end and red blue swapping. Five bit forms use one pad or alpha bit plus five bits per channel with the single bit at either end and similar swaps. Five six five forms devote five bits to red and blue and six to green without alpha.

Thirty two bit packed color provides eight bits per channel and ten bit variants little endian. Eight bit forms reserve eight bits each for pad or alpha plus red green blue, with the extra byte at either end and red blue order swapped across eight naming variants. Ten bit forms use two bits of pad or alpha plus ten bits per channel, or ten bits per channel plus two trailing bits, again with red blue order swapped.

Deep integer color uses sixteen bits per channel without compression little endian. Forty eight bit forms store red green blue sequentially with red first and blue first orderings. Sixty four bit forms add a sixteen bit pad or alpha channel before the same ordered triple, yielding four sixteen bit components.

Floating point color extends deep layouts to half and single precision little endian. Sixty four bit half forms mirror pad or alpha plus triple layouts but interpret channels as half floats, with red first and blue first orders plus single, dual and triple half variants. Single precision forms provide one, two, three and four thirty two bit float channels for red only, green red, blue green red and alpha blue green red layouts. A separate sixty four bit integer format interleaves ten bit alpha blue green red values each followed by six padding bits.

Packed eight bit YUV interleaves luma and chroma in thirty two or twenty four bit units little endian. Four two two variants order two luma samples with one Cb and one Cr sample in four permutations. Four four four variants store alpha or pad plus luma and chroma in normal or reversed chroma order, and a twenty four bit variant stores Cr Cb and luma without extra byte. Two further ten bit tags cover a non linear only use and a two ten ten ten packing of pad plus Cr Cb and luma.

Higher precision packed YUV extends interleaving to ten twelve and sixteen bits per component little endian. One group packs two luma samples plus Cb and Cr for two pixels into sixty four bits, using ten bits plus six padding, twelve bits plus four padding, or full sixteen bits per component. Another group packs alpha or pad plus Cr, luma and Cb into thirty two or sixty four bits with two ten ten ten, twelve plus padding, or full sixteen bit components, including wide chroma orders.

Four opaque tiled tags and two YUV four two zero tags appear only as identifiers without component description in the fragment, so memory layout cannot be derived here beyond distinct names. Eight further tags combine familiar base color names with a separate alpha suffix but likewise provide only identifiers here without explicit packing, plane count or alpha placement detail.

Semi planar YUV keeps luma in one plane and interleaved chroma in a second plane. Six eight bit variants differ by chroma sampling of two by two, two by one or none, and by Cr Cb versus Cb Cr order. Three ten bit variants repeat the same sampling choices for Cr Cb order. Further ten twelve and sixteen bit two plane families and packed ten bit two plane forms refine depth and packing, while three additional tags provide only identifiers without sampling or layout detail here.

Tri planar high depth YUV uses three separate planes for luma and chroma. Nine tags cover ten twelve and sixteen bits per channel, each depth offering two by two sampled, two by one sampled and non sampled chroma geometries with Cb in the second plane and Cr in the third.

Fully planar eight bit YUV separates luma and chroma into three planes with chroma order swapped between naming orders. Sampling spans four by four, four by one, two by two, two by one and non sampled geometries, each in both chroma orders. An eight bit luma only tag and a two ten ten ten tag packing pad plus three luma components complete the group.

Modifier vendor codes occupy a small integer namespace where absence is zero and twelve vendors take successive values one through twelve in order Intel, AMD, Nvidia, Samsung, Qualcomm, Vivante, Broadcom, ARM, Allwinner, Amlogic, MediaTek and Apple. The fragment defines only these vendor codes, not complete modifier values.
